references.text: In John 5:18, the same theme appears where the Jews seek to kill Jesus, but here the reason is that he made God his own Father and healed on the Sabbath.
In John 8:37-40, the Jews in Jerusalem resume their plans to kill Jesus, confirming that they know who he is and what he has said, yet they refuse to listen.
In John 11:53, the conspiracy against Jesus reaches its peak, as from that time on they decided to kill him, which is a direct result of the discussion in Jerusalem.
In John 10:31-33, the Jews pick up stones to stone Jesus, confirming that they know he is a man who makes himself God, showing that they have identified him as the one they seek to destroy.

In John 12:10-11, the conspiracy expands to include Lazarus as well, whom they plan to kill because he is living proof of Jesus' power, demonstrating that their fear of Jesus leads them to seek the death of anyone connected to him.
